title: Inconsistent Parameter Ordering (Connascence of Position)
pattern: Using different parameter ordering for identical logical arguments in parallel or related method signatures.
why_bad: It breaks the expected conceptual position. Because both parameters share the same type (`&str`), compilers cannot prevent accidental inversion, leading to silent database and logic bugs at runtime.
detection: Compare sibling functions that accept the same set of argument types but vary their relative positions.
counterexample: Functions where parameter order is explicitly bound by language trait contracts (e.g., standard library traits).
fix: Unify the parameter order across all signatures (e.g., always placing identity/name first, followed by options/details).
source: *Code Complete, Second Edition* by Steve McConnell (2004), p. 93-94, 627.
